summary.headline: Lumax Auto FY26 record consolidated revenue of INR 4,870 crore (+34%) and PAT of INR 337 crore (+47%), with EBITDA margin at 14.5%.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 4,870 crore and Q4 revenue of INR 1,417 crore, up 34% and 25% respectively. EBITDA reached INR 705 crore (14.5% margin) for FY26 and INR 208 crore (14.7%) in Q4. Q4 PAT was INR 98 crore, but the quarter was distorted by a reclassification of intangible asset lives (from the Greenfuel acquisition) that raised depreciation and cut minority share to 10%. Management guided to 20% revenue CAGR over the next 3 to 5 years and a margin uplift of at least 30 bps in FY27, while flagging cost inflation with a 3 to 6 month pass-through lag.

guidance_outlook: Mid-term strategy: 20% revenue CAGR over the next 3 to 5 years, a mix of organic and inorganic growth; some businesses targeted at 2x to 3x industry growth.
FY27 margin expected to sustain or improve by at least 30 bps, as inflation (raw materials, wages, energy) is passed back to OEMs with a 3 to 6 month lag.
FY27 capex guided at INR 275 crore to INR 300 crore.
Minority share expected at 15% to 17% for the full year, similar to last year.
Lumax Ituran FY27 EBITDA margin guided to improve by up to 150 bps.
Dividend payout minimum 35% maintained for FY26; FY27 payout policy to be reviewed.
Order book of INR 1,450 crore: about 25% to execute in FY27, 54% in FY28, 21% in FY29.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 233 crore, including INR 45 crore land in Gujarat and Kharkhoda and about INR 100 crore on capacity at IAC and Lumax Alps Alpine.
FY27 capex plan INR 275 crore to INR 300 crore, with new lines and machinery across verticals and a new Mechatronics facility.
Some verticals still run at 20% to 30% spare capacity; others need capacity ramp-up to meet order book.
New Bangalore R&D centre SHIFT (software-focused) has about 20 engineers; annual cost INR 5 crore to INR 7 crore.
BCM (Body Control Module) product entering SOP in 45 to 60 days.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth attributed to retail pull after GST rationalisation; management says Q1 FY27 demand remains intact with no significant OEM pullback.
Industry production in Q4 FY26 per SIAM: PV +11% to 15.7 lakh units; 2W +21% to 70.5 lakh; 3W +32% to 3.4 lakh; CV +20% to 3.6 lakh.
Input cost inflation (polypropylene, commodities, wages, energy) with back-to-back OEM recovery, lagging 3 to 6 months.
Labour shortages in April-May 2026 acknowledged; management said production impact was negligible.
Shift-by-wire AT shifters expected to migrate to e-shifters over about 36 months; SOPs already won on 3 platforms.
China office has about 8 staff, to grow to about 15, seeking technology tie-ups with local Chinese companies.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q4 growth, and what about Tata Motors appearing down 56% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 growth to retail demand after GST rationalisation. CFO said the Tata figure was a misreading; Tata grew about 33-34% in the prior-year Q4, in line with OEM growth of 34%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the consolidated margin guidance intact given raw material and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflation is largely recovered from OEMs with a 3 to 6 month lag. Management expects FY27 margins to sustain or rise by at least 30 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit Lumax JOPP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JOPP was a very small revenue contributor and a continuing drag on profit, so resources are being redirected to businesses with scale and margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and standalone debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated debt is about INR 1,000 crore, of which long-term is about INR 550 to 570 crore. More than 90% of the long-term debt funds acquisitions; full repayment starts in FY27 and debt is expected to decline over 3 to 4 years. Standalone numbers rose because IAC and Lumax Ancillary were merged in.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend payout ratio and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The minimum 35% payout is maintained for FY26, based on standalone profit. The CFO said FY27 payout will be reviewed and revisited next year.

qa_highlights.question: Non-current investments rose from INR 162 crore to INR 312.6 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the mark-to-market gain on the 5% stake in Lumax Industries Limited, as its share price rose.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% CAGR inclusive of inorganic growth, and how will minority interest move?
qa_highlights.answer: The 20% CAGR is a mix of organic and inorganic growth; no timing is set for the next acquisition. Minority share is expected at 15% to 17% for FY27; the Q4 10% figure was exceptional due to the intangible reclassification.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT and minority share distorted by intangible asset reclassification; watch whether Q1 FY27 depreciation normalises.
Raw material, wage and energy inflation with a 3 to 6 month lag before OEM pass-through; margin guidance depends on recoveries.
IAC concentration: over 90% of its order book is from M&M; new OEM wins are not expected until FY28 to FY29.
Lumax Mannoh growing about 9% to 10% in FY26, lagging other subsidiaries of 20% to 25%; Lumax Ituran EBITDA margin dipped in FY26 and is guided up 150 bps in FY27.
Pending exits and acquisitions: sale of 50% in Lumax JOPP to JOPP Holding Germany and purchase of the remaining 15.97% in Lumax FAE, subject to conditions.
CNG supply constraints reported by dealers; management says CNG demand remains strong.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and the 20% CAGR target, but cautious on macro volatility, input cost inflation and labour availability. Management was evasive on specific FY27 growth numbers for IAC and the next inorganic deal, saying it was too volatile to quantify.
key_quotes: I'm pleased to share that the Company delivered its best ever financial and operational performance in FY 26, with revenue reaching an all-time high of INR 4,870 crore.
we continue to be on par with the mid-term strategy of our 20% CAGR over the next 3 to 5 years.
Mahindra will continue to dominate the lion's share of IAC's pie.
I do not foresee any reason that the margins would get negatively impacted.
